stage: Stage 4 — inventory master + per-BOM stock check
intro: Request-level test cases for the Stage-4 inventory API: the stock master sync (dry-run preview and idempotent commit), the stock list, and the per-BOM inventory check that reserves stock and produces the shortfall lines Stage 5 turns into supplier POs.
notes: **MD and DM bypass every `require_roles` gate** (`SUPERUSER_ROLES` in `app/modules/users/deps.py`). Use the Cutting Manager or Office Viewer for wrong-role cases on the mutating routes; the Office Viewer is *inside* the read gate, so use the Cutting Manager for wrong-role reads.
Two error shapes: `{"detail": "..."}` for 404s, role 403s and the 413 upload cap; `{"error": "...", "message": "..."}` for the service's own refusals (`bom_not_approved`).
The check runs only on an **approved, locked or exported** BOM — `_APPROVED_STATES`. A draft or ready-for-review BOM is refused.

Only stockable categories are checked: main material, sub material, lining, interlining, thread, accessory, packaging. Anything else (labour, overhead, …) is carried as `excluded` rather than being matched.

A re-run first **releases** that BOM's previous reservations (reason `recheck`), then re-claims — so re-running never double-counts the BOM against itself, but reservations held by *other* BOMs do reduce what this one can see.
A fuzzy match is only ever a **suggestion**: flags carry `suggestion` + `unmatched` and `matched_method` stays null. Only an exact normalized key or a curated alias binds automatically.
There is no endpoint to release a reservation, confirm a suggestion or set a manual match — everything here is driven by re-running the check. Treat that as a coverage gap, not a missing test.

cases.title: Preview a stock workbook
steps: multipart body: file = <the stock master workbook>
cases.expected: 200 with the preview block — parsed row count, warnings and samples. Nothing is written: a follow-up GET /inventory/items is unchanged.

cases.title: Commit the stock workbook
cases.expected: 200 with the preview block plus committed: N and deactivated: M. Items are upserted on normalized_key with description, uom, qty_on_hand, rate and color.

cases.title: Wrong role commits
cases.expected: 403 role-not-permitted — the sync is DM/MD only.

cases.title: A viewer cannot commit
cases.expected: 403 — the Office Viewer can read the stock list (B-P3) but is outside the mutating gate. This pair is the clearest read/write split in the module.

cases.title: No file part
cases.expected: 422 — File(...) is required.

cases.title: Upload over the cap
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/inventory/preview — file = <larger than MAX_UPLOAD_MB (25 MB default)>
cases.expected: 413 {"detail":"File exceeds the 25 MB limit."} — raised while streaming by this module's own _read_capped, independent of the Stage-1 upload machinery.

cases.title: Empty or unparseable workbook
cases.expected: Expect a clean 4xx or a preview with warnings and zero rows — NOT a 500. There is no content-type check on this route, so the parser is the only guard; record what actually happens.

cases.title: Commit an empty but valid workbook
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/inventory/commit with a structurally valid workbook containing NO data rows
cases.expected: committed: 0 and deactivated: <every previously active key> — because `deactivate_keys_not_in(keep)` runs with an empty keep-set. One wrong file can retire the entire stock master. Confirm and flag loudly; this is the highest-blast-radius call in the module.

cases.title: Commit is idempotent
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/inventory/commit twice with the identical file
cases.expected: The second commit reports the same `committed` count and deactivated: 0; no duplicate items appear — the upsert keys on normalized_key.

cases.title: Missing keys are deactivated, not deleted
steps: Commit workbook v2 which omits one previously present item
cases.expected: `deactivated` counts it and the row still exists (inactive) — history and any reservations against it survive. Confirm whether the list endpoint hides inactive items by default.

cases.title: Preview and commit agree
steps: POST /inventory/preview with a file and note the row count and warnings
cases.expected: commit's preview block matches preview's exactly, and `committed` equals the previewed row count — the dry run is trustworthy as a go/no-go.

cases.title: List stock items
cases.expected: 200 {"items":[{id,normalized_key,description,uom,qty_on_hand,rate,color,…}], "count": N}.

cases.title: Search the master
cases.expected: 200; every row matches the search term. `count` is this page's length, not the total.

cases.title: Office Viewer can read stock
cases.expected: 200 — VIEWER is inside the _VIEW gate.

cases.title: Role outside the read gate
cases.expected: 403 role-not-permitted — worth noting that the manager who consumes the stock cannot query it here.

cases.title: No token
cases.expected: 401 — unlike the supplier-PO tracking routes, nothing in this module is anonymous.

cases.title: limit=0 and a far offset
cases.expected: 200 with an empty list both times — limit and offset have no bounds or validation.

cases.title: Unbounded limit
cases.expected: 200, accepted — no server-side ceiling. Flag as a perf gap on a large master.

cases.title: Are deactivated items listed?
steps: Commit a workbook that drops an item (A-L2)
cases.expected: Determine from the response whether inactive rows are included — there is no `active` filter on this endpoint, unlike GET /suppliers. If they are listed with no status flag, a picker cannot tell live stock from retired stock; file that.

cases.title: Check an approved BOM
cases.expected: 200 with the check: a header plus one line per stockable BOM item carrying required_qty, on_hand_qty, shortfall_qty, status (sufficient / partial / out_of_stock), matched_method and flags. Active reservations are created for whatever could be claimed.

cases.title: Check a locked or exported BOM
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/boms/{bom_id}/inventory-check on a BOM whose status is locked, then on one that is exported
cases.expected: 200 both times — _APPROVED_STATES covers approved, locked and exported.

cases.title: Re-run the check
steps: Commit a stock file that raises the on-hand quantity
cases.expected: 200; the second check reflects the new stock and the BOM's own earlier reservations do not count against it — they are released with reason `recheck` before re-claiming.

cases.title: Check an unapproved BOM
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/boms/{bom_id}/inventory-check on a BOM in draft or ready_for_review
cases.expected: 409 {"error":"bom_not_approved","message":"Inventory check runs only on an approved/locked BOM."}

cases.title: Check a rejected BOM
cases.expected: 409 bom_not_approved — rejected is not in _APPROVED_STATES either.

cases.title: Unknown BOM
cases.expected: 404 {"detail":"BOM not found."}

cases.title: Wrong role runs the check
cases.expected: 403 — running a check writes reservations, so it sits behind the mutating gate.

cases.title: A BOM with no stockable lines
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/boms/{bom_id}/inventory-check on a BOM whose lines are all non-stockable categories
cases.expected: 200 with no checked lines and everything reported as excluded — no error, and generate-pos on it should then yield an empty PO list.

cases.title: A line whose required quantity is 0
steps: Leave a stockable BOM line at qty_per_garment 0
cases.expected: That line cannot be `sufficient` — the sufficiency test requires required > 0 — so a zero-requirement line lands on out_of_stock (or partial) with shortfall 0. Confirm, and flag it: a 0-qty line reads as a stock problem when it is really an unfilled BOM cell.

cases.title: UOM mismatch with no conversion
steps: Have a BOM line in a UOM that has no conversion to the matched stock item's UOM (e.g. sqft vs. metres)
cases.expected: The line carries flags containing `uom_mismatch`, on_hand_qty 0 and status out_of_stock — an unconvertible lot is treated as no stock rather than silently compared. Verify no reservation was made against that lot.

cases.title: Exactly enough stock
steps: Set a stock item's qty_on_hand exactly equal to the BOM line's requirement
cases.expected: status sufficient with shortfall_qty 0 — the comparison is available >= required, so the exact boundary passes rather than falling to partial.

cases.title: Another BOM's reservation reduces what you can claim
steps: Run the check on BOM A so it reserves most of a lot
Run the check on BOM B, which needs the same material
Compare BOM B's on_hand_qty with its available/shortfall
cases.expected: BOM B sees the lot's on-hand but an `available` reduced by A's active reservation, so it reports partial or out_of_stock with a real shortfall. This is the whole point of soft reservations — two BOMs cannot both spend the same leather.

cases.title: A fuzzy candidate never auto-binds
steps: Have a BOM line whose name only loosely resembles a stock description (no exact key, no alias)
cases.expected: flags contain `suggestion` and `unmatched`, the suggestion payload names the candidate, matched_method is null and no stock is claimed. A human must curate an alias before it counts — verify the line is short (not silently satisfied).

cases.title: An alias binds where the raw key does not
steps: Note a line that comes back unmatched
Add a curated alias mapping that BOM term to the stock key
cases.expected: matched_method becomes `alias`, the line matches the lot and stock is reserved — the documented path from an unmatched line to a satisfied one.

cases.title: The check is Stage 5's precondition
steps: On a freshly approved BOM, POST /api/v1/procurement/boms/{bom_id}/generate-pos → 409 no_inventory_check
cases.expected: The PO generation that was refused now succeeds and buys exactly the lines this check marked short. This is the seam between Stage 4 and Stage 5 — run it end to end at least once.

cases.title: Read one check by id
cases.expected: 200 — the rebuilt check view with every line, its status, flags and matched item.

cases.title: The dashboard
cases.expected: 200 — the latest check per BOM, grouped with client and order identity; the filtered call narrows to one order.

cases.title: Latest check for a BOM
cases.expected: 200 — the same view as D-P1 for that BOM's most recent check.

cases.title: Office Viewer can read checks
cases.expected: 200 — reads are open to VIEWER across this module.

cases.title: Unknown check id
cases.expected: 404 {"detail":"Inventory check not found."}

cases.title: A BOM that was never checked
steps: GET /api/v1/procurement/boms/{bom_id}/inventory-check on a BOM with no check
cases.expected: 404 {"detail":"No inventory check for this BOM yet."} — a distinct message from D-N1, and the signal a UI should read as "run the check" rather than "something broke".

cases.title: Malformed id
cases.expected: 422 from FastAPI's path parsing, before the handler runs.

cases.title: Wrong role reads a check
cases.expected: 403 role-not-permitted.

cases.title: "Latest" really is the latest
steps: Run a check, note its id from the response
cases.expected: The returned check id is the SECOND run's, not the first — and the older check is still readable by id via D-P1, so the history of what was decided is preserved.

cases.title: The dashboard shows one row per BOM
steps: Run checks on several BOMs, re-running one of them twice
cases.expected: Exactly one row per BOM, carrying the latest run — the board is a current-state view, not a log.
